source.title: The Tangled Web They Weave: Exploring Neural Representations with Directed Simplicial Complexes

record.tranche_reason: The paper uses distributed representations and polysemanticity as motivation for a method to map causal interactions among neurons. Its experiments evaluate that method on small MLPs; they do not test the claim versions about superposition, capacity allocation, LLM features, SAE units, or feature dimensionality.
record.gate_note: The reported results measure properties of directed simplicial complexes (DSCs), not whether features are stored as overlapping near-orthogonal directions or whether capacity pressure causes polysemanticity. The paper itself says that whether DSCs identify polysemantic neurons remains open. Comparisons with circuit-discovery methods are not claim-version tests.
record.test_reason: The paper proposes a DSC method for describing multi-neuron causal interactions and evaluates it on handcrafted, trained and untrained quadrant-classifier MLPs. Its results are properties of the DSCs: simplex counts, dimensions, Jaccard distances and agreement with circuit methods. It does not measure feature geometry, sparsity transitions, capacity allocation, LLM or SAE features, or feature dimensionality. The polysemantic network is polysemantic by construction, and the authors say semantics are their own assignment. They also leave open whether DSCs identify polysemantic neurons.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. Authors present DSCs as context-dependent descriptions of multi-neuron computation that recover designed pathways and agree with circuit methods on representable edges. They leave open whether DSCs identify polysemantic neurons and whether higher-dimensional simplices reflect genuine higher-order interactions.
record.recipe_differences: The study constructs context-dependent filtered directed simplicial complexes from coherent counterfactual ablations and target-activation relevance tests; it does not reproduce the Toy Models of Superposition method or measure its feature-direction geometry.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported construction is somewhat sensitive to input distribution and selection tolerance. Sample size changes complex size; multiple-testing correction affects some trained-network complexes, including the trained [2, 3, 4, 4] Q3 case; integration step can shift filtration values and reverse simplex ordering.

fits_no_version.finding: DSCs recover designed pathways in handcrafted quadrant classifiers. Trained and untrained nets give larger, higher-dimensional complexes, so size does not show learned structure.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Context-dependent causal-complex measurements describe multi-neuron computation in small MLPs, but complex size alone does not indicate learned feature organization.

fits_no_version.finding: Maximal-simplex membership singles out the Q4 neuron n7 (14), not the six coordinate-mixing neurons (2–7).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: DSC participation counts do not identify polysemantic neurons in a constructed network.

record.problems: Experiments are limited to small ReLU MLPs on a synthetic two-dimensional classification task. The authors say that whether DSCs identify polysemantic neurons remains open and that their relevance test does not compare joint effects with individual-predictor effects. Candidate counts limit scalability; multiple-testing error is not controlled jointly across dimensions, input sets, and networks.
record.rows_left_out: Appendices H and I report context-distance and circuit-method comparisons, but these do not measure the claim versions' feature geometry, capacity account, LLM features, SAE units, or feature dimensionality. Other parameter-sensitivity results are not included because they concern DSC construction settings rather than those claim versions.

untested.parts: Sparse features exceeding dimensions, near-orthogonal overlapping directions, sparsity-dependent transition, regular geometry.
Whether capacity limits cause polysemanticity. The [2,3,4,4] bottleneck is handcrafted, not learned under capacity pressure.
Origins of polysemanticity without capacity pressure. Footnote 5 notes that mono/polysemantic labels depend on basis choice, but no result tests this.
LLM neuron spread and SAE-recoverable features.

record.verdict_notes: Not an original source. Mono/polysemantic labels are by construction and basis-dependent (footnote 5, Appendix C.1). No row bears on any version; all rows correctly set to none. The Appendix H and I comparisons concern the method's own validation and are rightly left out.

versions.untested_parts: Sparse features exceeding network dimensions, overlap and near-orthogonal feature geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether limited capacity causes polysemanticity, and whether feature importance determines which features get dedicated dimensions or share.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise without capacity pressure. Randomly initialized networks are included, but their feature semantics are not established.
LLM representations, neuron-spread measurements, and SAE-recoverable sparse features.
Whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
Whether superposed features are one-dimensional directions or multidimensional.

rows.subject: handcrafted monosemantic [2, 4, 4, 4] network
rows.operation_detail: Constructed a DSC for each one-hot quadrant input set and counted its simplices.
rows.value: Each of the four DSCs contains ten edges and four 2-simplices; they coincide up to relabelling.
rows.note: Measures context-dependent causal structure in a network whose feature computations were designed in advance; it does not measure superposition geometry.

rows.subject: handcrafted polysemantic [2, 3, 4, 4] network
rows.operation_detail: Constructed DSCs for one-hot quadrant input sets and counted their simplices.
rows.value: The one-hot DSCs contain between four and twelve edges and between two and four 2-simplices.
rows.note: The first-layer bottleneck and mixed-coordinate units are specified by construction. These DSC counts do not test whether capacity pressure explains polysemanticity.

rows.subject: handcrafted polysemantic [2, 3, 4, 4] network
rows.operation_detail: Counted maximal-simplex memberships of neurons across the four one-hot DSCs.

conditions.value: four one-hot quadrant sets, combined for the reported membership counts

rows.measure: Number of maximal simplices containing each neuron
rows.value: n7 belongs to 14 maximal simplices across the four complexes; each of the six neurons described as mixing both coordinates belongs to between two and seven.
rows.note: The authors say this count does not identify the polysemantic neurons; its interpretation also depends on the chosen elementary features.

rows.subject: trained [2, 4, 4, 4] network
rows.operation_detail: Constructed DSCs for one-hot quadrant input sets and counted simplices and maximum dimension.
rows.baseline: Handcrafted network of the same architecture: 22 simplices per quadrant; maximum dimension two.
rows.value: Trained complexes contain 24, 220, 132, and 38 simplices for Q1–Q4; maximum dimensions are 2, 4, 4, and 3, respectively.
rows.note: Complex size and dimension are measurements of the proposed DSC representation, not measurements of feature overlap or its geometry.
rows.check: Value and baseline match Table 2. These are measurements of the study's own method on a trained toy net, not a superposition measure.

rows.subject: trained [2, 3, 4, 4] network
rows.operation_detail: Constructed DSCs for one-hot quadrant input sets and counted simplices and maximum dimension.
rows.baseline: Handcrafted network of the same architecture: 13–23 simplices; maximum dimension two.
rows.value: Trained complexes contain 365, 346, 87, and 32 simplices for Q1–Q4; maximum dimensions are 4, 4, 3, and 3, respectively.
rows.note: Complex size and dimension do not establish that the network learned the structure or that it reflects superposition.
rows.check: Matches Table 2. This is a measure of the method's own output only.

rows.subject: untrained [2, 4, 4, 4] networks
rows.operation_detail: Constructed DSCs on the trained network's one-hot input sets and compared their sizes with trained-network complexes.

conditions.value: one-hot Q1–Q4 of the trained network

rows.measure: DSC size compared with the trained network for the same quadrant
rows.value: Five of twelve untrained complexes are larger than the trained complex of the same quadrant; sizes for Q2 range from 8 to 419 across seeds.
rows.note: The authors conclude that complex size does not show that its structure was learned.

rows.subject: untrained [2, 3, 4, 4] networks
rows.operation_detail: Constructed DSCs on the trained network's one-hot input sets and compared their sizes with trained-network complexes.

conditions.value: one-hot Q1–Q4 of the trained network

rows.measure: DSC size compared with the trained network for the same quadrant
rows.value: All twelve untrained complexes are smaller than the corresponding trained complexes; the largest untrained complex has 327 simplices, compared with 346 for the trained Q2 complex.
rows.note: The authors compare sizes only and caution that this does not establish feature semantics.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
